previous_findings.evidence: §44 separates application DB-open counts from recovery counters. FI-DB-01a/01b permit at most one mode=ro recovery connection with only the two fixed PRAGMAs; FI-DB-01c forbids opening an untrusted identity-mismatched object.
FI-CLEAN-01 enumerates all legal cleanup source states and distinguishes zero-byte/no-frame, complete-frame, and partial-frame restart outcomes; deletion requires durable cleanup_quarantined.

passed: §63 defines the verified catalog.log handle as the unique global catalog lock object and bootstrap lock serializes first creation; ordinary operations do not wait on bootstrap, so the lock order has no cycle.
Advisory catalog read -> release -> stable case lock -> catalog re-read under lock -> release -> OpenVerified is consistently specified; same-case mutations hold the case lock.
Per-state capabilities and cleanup source transitions are consistent with docs/41 §109.2.
Absent-directory cleanup verifies and syncs the pinned parent before the deleted tombstone while retaining the external stable case lock, consistent with docs/41 §109.3.

Normal CaseHandle.Close releases the case lock last; CleanupCase keeps that lock through durable quarantine, member/directory deletion, and tombstone; Supervisor.Close owns only shared-resource closure.
An unknown lower-level close state requires the dedicated pilot child to exit and its PID to be reaped before a replacement child starts; unknown handles are never closed again in-process.
